subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Reko Diq is famous for its deposits of:
explanation: Reko Diq is one of the world’s largest undeveloped copper-gold deposits.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Reko Diq is located in the district of:
explanation: Reko Diq lies in the Chagai hills of north-western Balochistan near the Iran and Afghanistan borders.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Saindak mine in Chagai, run by a Chinese company, mainly produces:
explanation: Saindak’s copper-gold ore is processed into blister copper that also contains gold and silver.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Duddar mine in Lasbela district produces:
explanation: Duddar in Lasbela is Pakistan’s main lead–zinc mine, developed with Chinese investment.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Khewra Salt Mine lies in the:
explanation: Khewra, in Jhelum district, has been mined for rock salt since Mughal times and is the source of much ‘Himalayan’ pink salt.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Muslim Bagh in Balochistan is known for deposits of:
explanation: The Muslim Bagh ophiolite in Killa Saifullah district holds Pakistan’s best-known chromite deposits.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Kalabagh and Chiniot are known for deposits of:
explanation: Iron ore is found at Kalabagh in Mianwali and in the Rajoa area of Chiniot.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Swat is famous for deposits of:
explanation: Emerald mines near Mingora in Swat produce green gemstones of high quality.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Hunza Valley is known for which gemstone?
explanation: Marble-hosted rubies are mined in the hills of Hunza in Gilgit-Baltistan; emeralds come from Swat and pink topaz from Katlang.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Koh-e-Sultan in Chagai is known for deposits of:
explanation: Koh-e-Sultan is an extinct volcano in Chagai district where sulphur has been mined.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Billion Tree Tsunami afforestation drive was launched in 2014 in:
explanation: The provincial government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa launched the campaign in 2014; it later grew into the national Ten Billion Tree Tsunami.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan became a member of the UN in:
explanation: Pakistan was admitted to the United Nations on 30 September 1947, about six weeks after independence.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which country voted against Pakistan’s admission to the United Nations in 1947?
explanation: Afghanistan cast the only vote against, citing its claims over the Pashtun areas, though it withdrew the objection soon afterwards.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which Pakistani diplomat served as the President of the United Nations (UN) General Assembly?
explanation: Sir Muhammad Zafrulla Khan presided over the 17th session of the General Assembly in 1962–63 and later headed the International Court of Justice.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The first country to recognise Pakistan after independence was:
explanation: Iran was the first state to recognise Pakistan in August 1947, and the Shah later became the first foreign head of state to visit.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The first foreign head of state to pay an official visit to Pakistan (1950) was:
explanation: Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi visited Pakistan in March 1950, reflecting the close early ties between the two neighbours.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Liaquat Ali Khan’s first official visit abroad as Prime Minister (1950) was to the:
explanation: Liaquat visited the United States in May 1950 instead of the Soviet Union, an early signal of Pakistan’s Western alignment.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan’s first ambassador to the United States was:
explanation: Mirza Abol Hassan Ispahani, a close associate of Quaid-i-Azam, served in Washington from 1947 to 1952.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan signed the Mutual Defence Assistance Agreement with the United States in:
explanation: The May 1954 agreement opened the way for US military aid and preceded Pakistan’s entry into SEATO and the Baghdad Pact.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan joined SEATO in:
explanation: Pakistan signed the Manila Pact that created the South-East Asia Treaty Organization in September 1954.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Southeast Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO) formally came to an end in:
explanation: SEATO was dissolved in June 1977 after its members lost interest following the Vietnam War; Pakistan had already left in the early 1970s.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan joined the Baghdad Pact in:
explanation: Pakistan joined Turkey, Iraq, Britain and Iran in the Baghdad Pact in 1955.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Baghdad Pact was renamed CENTO in 1959 after the withdrawal of:
explanation: After Iraq’s 1958 revolution and its withdrawal, the alliance became the Central Treaty Organization.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: After 1958 the headquarters of the Baghdad Pact/CENTO was moved to:
explanation: Following the revolution in Iraq, the secretariat moved from Baghdad to Ankara.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: CENTO was dissolved in:
explanation: CENTO collapsed in 1979 when Iran, after its revolution, and Pakistan withdrew.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The American U-2 spy plane shot down over the Soviet Union in 1960 had flown from:
explanation: Gary Powers’ U-2 took off from Peshawar (Badaber), and Khrushchev warned Pakistan of the consequences.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan joined the Non-Aligned Movement in:
explanation: Pakistan joined NAM at the Havana summit of 1979, after leaving CENTO.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan left the Commonwealth in 1972 and rejoined it in:
explanation: Pakistan left when Britain moved to recognise Bangladesh and rejoined in October 1989 during Benazir Bhutto’s government.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan is a founding member of the D-8, a grouping of:
explanation: The D-8 Organization for Economic Cooperation was founded in 1997 by eight developing Muslim countries including Pakistan, Turkey, Iran and Egypt.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Kashmir dispute was taken to the UN Security Council in January 1948 by:
explanation: India referred the issue to the Security Council on 1 January 1948, which later passed resolutions calling for a plebiscite.

subject: Pakistan Affairs

o: partition of Kashmir along the Chenab
a plebiscite in Jammu and Kashmir
explanation: UNCIP resolutions of 13 August 1948 and 5 January 1949 called for a ceasefire followed by a free and impartial plebiscite.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The ceasefire line in Kashmir was first laid down by the:
explanation: Military representatives signed the Karachi Agreement in July 1949 under UN auspices, fixing the ceasefire line.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: UNMOGIP is a UN mission that monitors the:
explanation: The UN Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan has observed the ceasefire in Kashmir since 1949.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The ceasefire line in Kashmir was renamed the Line of Control under the:
explanation: The Simla Agreement of 1972 converted the 1971 ceasefire line into the Line of Control.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Kashmir Solidarity Day is observed in Pakistan on:
explanation: Pakistan observes 5 February every year to express support for the people of Indian-administered Kashmir.

subject: Pakistan Affairs

explanation: Pakistan downgraded diplomatic ties and suspended bilateral trade after India’s move of 5 August 2019.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pervez Musharraf gave a ______-point formula for the solution of Kashmir.
explanation: Musharraf’s four-point proposal (2006) envisaged demilitarisation, self-governance, soft borders and a joint supervision mechanism.

subject: Pakistan Affairs

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Simla Agreement of 1972 was signed by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and:
explanation: Bhutto and Indira Gandhi signed the agreement at Simla in July 1972 after the 1971 war.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Lahore Declaration of February 1999 was signed by Nawaz Sharif and:
explanation: Vajpayee travelled to Lahore by bus, and the two prime ministers agreed on nuclear confidence-building and dialogue.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Agra Summit of July 2001 was held between Pervez Musharraf and:
explanation: The summit ended without a joint declaration, mainly over differences on Kashmir.

subject: Pakistan Affairs

explanation: The Delhi agreement completed the return of Pakistani prisoners of war held since 1971.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Rann of Kutch dispute was settled by an international tribunal in:
explanation: After fighting in 1965, the case went to a tribunal whose 1968 award gave Pakistan about a tenth of the disputed area.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Sir Creek dispute concerns a tidal estuary between Sindh and India’s state of:
explanation: Sir Creek lies in the marshes of the Rann of Kutch; the dispute also affects maritime boundaries in the Arabian Sea.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Kartarpur Corridor, opened in 2019, gives Sikh pilgrims visa-free access to a gurdwara in the district of:
explanation: Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur in Narowal, where Guru Nanak spent his last years, is linked to Dera Baba Nanak in India.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Under an agreement of 1988, Pakistan and India exchange lists of their nuclear installations every year on:
explanation: The Agreement on the Prohibition of Attack against Nuclear Installations requires an annual exchange of lists on 1 January.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan and China signed their boundary agreement in:
explanation: The agreement of March 1963 settled the border between Gilgit-Baltistan and Xinjiang.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan established diplomatic relations with the People’s Republic of China in:
explanation: Pakistan recognised the PRC in January 1950 and established formal diplomatic relations on 21 May 1951.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan facilitated Henry Kissinger’s secret trip to Beijing in:
explanation: In July 1971 Kissinger flew to Beijing from Pakistan, paving the way for Nixon’s visit to China in 1972.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The second OIC summit was held in 1974 at:
explanation: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto hosted the Islamic Summit in Lahore in February 1974.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan recognised Bangladesh in:
explanation: Pakistan recognised Bangladesh in February 1974, on the eve of the Lahore Islamic Summit.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The OIC Contact Group on Jammu and Kashmir was established in:
explanation: The Contact Group was formed in 1994 to coordinate the OIC’s position on Kashmir and meets regularly on the sidelines of OIC and UN sessions.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: COMSTECH, the OIC standing committee on science and technology, is chaired by the:
explanation: COMSTECH was set up in 1981 with its secretariat in Islamabad and the President of Pakistan as its chairman.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Lyallpur was renamed Faisalabad in honour of:
explanation: The city was renamed in 1977 in tribute to King Faisal bin Abdulaziz, a close friend of Pakistan, who was assassinated in 1975.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Which retired Pakistani army chief became the first commander of the Saudi-led Islamic Military Counter Terrorism Coalition?
explanation: General (retd) Raheel Sharif took command of the Riyadh-based coalition in 2017.

subject: Pakistan Affairs

explanation: The three RCD members revived their cooperation as ECO in 1985; seven more states joined in 1992.

subject: Pakistan Affairs

explanation: The Regional Cooperation for Development, formed by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey in 1964, became ECO in 1985.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The secretariat of ECO is located in:
explanation: ECO’s permanent secretariat is in Tehran; its cultural institute is also in Tehran and its science foundation in Islamabad.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: How many member states does ECO have?
explanation: Afghanistan and six Central Asian and Caucasian republics joined the three founders in 1992, making ten members.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The ECO Trade Agreement (ECOTA) was signed in 2003 at:
explanation: ECOTA was signed in Islamabad in July 2003 to reduce tariffs on trade among ECO members.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: SAARC was established in 1985 at:
explanation: The SAARC Charter was signed at the first summit in Dhaka on 8 December 1985 by seven South Asian states, including Pakistan.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The SAARC secretariat is located in:
explanation: The secretariat was set up in Kathmandu in 1987.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Afghanistan became the eighth member of SAARC in:
explanation: Afghanistan was admitted at the 14th SAARC summit in New Delhi in April 2007.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) agreement was signed at the SAARC summit held in 2004 in:
explanation: SAFTA was signed at the 12th SAARC summit in Islamabad in January 2004.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The 19th SAARC Summit, postponed in 2016, was to be held in:
explanation: India and several other members pulled out of the Islamabad summit in 2016, and no SAARC summit has been held since.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan became a permanent member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization in:
explanation: Pakistan and India were admitted as full members at the SCO summit in Astana in June 2017.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan was granted observer status in the SCO in:
explanation: Pakistan, India and Iran became SCO observers at the Astana summit of 2005; Pakistan became a full member in 2017.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: In 2017, Pakistan became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO). What is the primary purpose of the SCO?
o: To facilitate trade among member countries only
To establish a common currency for member states
To promote regional cooperation and stability in Eurasia
To operate a joint military command
explanation: The SCO focuses on security, political and economic cooperation in Eurasia, especially against terrorism, separatism and extremism.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The ‘three evils’ that the SCO aims to combat are terrorism, separatism and:
explanation: The Shanghai Convention of 2001 committed members to fight terrorism, separatism and extremism.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The SCO’s Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) is based in:
explanation: RATS, the SCO’s permanent counter-terrorism body, has its executive committee in Tashkent; the general secretariat is in Beijing.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan has been a member of the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) since:
explanation: Pakistan joined the ARF, Asia’s main security dialogue forum, in July 2004.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan became a Sectoral Dialogue Partner of ASEAN in:
explanation: ASEAN granted Pakistan sectoral dialogue partnership in 1993, before its entry into the ARF.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Durand Line agreement between British India and Afghanistan was signed in:
explanation: Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan signed the agreement in Kabul in November 1893.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Durand Line agreement was signed by Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir:
explanation: Amir Abdur Rahman Khan agreed the frontier with the British envoy in 1893.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The first Afghan Transit Trade Agreement between Pakistan and Afghanistan was signed in:
explanation: The 1965 agreement gave landlocked Afghanistan transit through Karachi; it was replaced by APTTA in 2010.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Afghanistan-Pakistan Transit Trade Agreement (APTTA) was signed in:
explanation: APTTA, signed in October 2010, replaced the 1965 agreement and allowed Afghan trucks access to Pakistani ports.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Soviet troops entered Afghanistan in:
explanation: The Soviet intervention of December 1979 made Pakistan a frontline state and brought millions of Afghan refugees.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: The Geneva Accords providing for Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan were signed in:
explanation: Pakistan and Afghanistan signed the Accords in April 1988, with the USA and USSR as guarantors; withdrawal was completed in February 1989.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Besides Pakistan, which two countries recognised the Taliban government of Afghanistan in 1997?
explanation: Only Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates recognised the first Taliban regime.

subject: Pakistan Affairs
q: Pakistan released Afghan Taliban leader ______ in 2018.
explanation: Mullah Abdul Ghani Baradar, held since 2010, was freed in 2018 to help the US–Taliban talks that led to the Doha Agreement.
